result.question: We have a rule for Transformer 1 at MAIN: if it reaches IEEE C57.104 Condition 3, we plan an outage and go to monthly oil sampling. Check whether we're there. Work out TDCG from the latest oil sample using hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene and co only. Use these limits: Condition 1 up to 720 ppm, Condition 2 from 721 to 1920, Condition 3 from 1921 to 4630, and Condition 4 above 4630. If it's Condition 3 or 4, do the following. Look at the MAIN schedule for the 21 days after the latest sample date and propose the 2-day outage window with the fewest scheduled work orders. Create a priority 1 outage and inspection work order for that window, with a note to notify the manufacturer. Create a separate work order for the next monthly DGA sample, dated 30 days after the latest sample. If it's Condition 2, don't plan an outage. Just create a quarterly resample work order. If it's Condition 1, create nothing and tell me how many ppm of headroom we have to 1921. In every case, first check for open work orders on Transformer 1 that already cover an outage or DGA sampling, and don't duplicate them. If one exists, reference it and explain how your recommendation differs. If any of the six gases is null in the latest sample, use its most recent non-null value and flag it as carried forward.
result.answer:
Transformer 1 is at **Condition 4**, a step past Condition 3, so your outage and monthly-sampling rule applies. I couldn't create either work order: the work-order system returned **403 Forbidden** on both attempts (the second time I set the WO number myself). Nothing was written, and the two work orders below are still open actions.

**TDCG from the latest oil sample (2024-01-19)**
| Gas | ppm |
|---|---|
| Hydrogen | 2,850 |
| Methane | 7,400 |
| Ethane | 5,470 |
| Ethylene | 16,650 |
| Acetylene | 7 |
| CO | 32 |
| **TDCG** | **32,409** |

- That is about seven times the 4,630 ppm Condition 4 limit.
- All six gases had values in this sample, so nothing was carried forward.
- This sample is about 2.7 years old (today is 2026-09-30), and it is the newest one on record.

**Open work orders on Transformer 1**
- **1000052**: a one-off oil retest (DGA) and insulation check. It's priority 3, awaiting approval, with a target start of 2026-10-01 and failure code FC006 (overheating). This already covers DGA sampling, so I didn't plan a separate sample work order. It differs from your rule in three ways:
  - It's one retest at priority 3, not a recurring monthly sample.
  - It was written for a T2 thermal fault (300–700 °C), without reference to the Condition 4 level.
  - Its date doesn't match the monthly schedule (next sample due 2024-02-18).
  - I recommend changing it to a monthly recurring sample and raising its priority.
- **1000051**: a priority 1 on-load tap changer inspection. It doesn't mention an outage, so it doesn't cover one. I recommend doing it during the planned outage.

**Work orders still to create (not created)**
1. **Priority 1 outage and inspection**
   - Proposed window: **2024-01-20 to 2024-01-21**. MAIN had no work orders scheduled anywhere in the 21 days from 2024-01-20 to 2024-02-09, so I picked the earliest two days.
   - Note to include: notify the manufacturer before the outage, and carry out the tap changer inspection in 1000051 during it.
2. **Next monthly DGA sample, dated 2024-02-18**
   - Only needed if you'd rather have this than update 1000052. Creating both would duplicate the sampling work.

Both work orders can be created once write access to the work-order system is restored.

Because these dates are in the past, you'll probably want to move the outage to the first open two-day window from today.
